name: Jehn's adversarial coin-basket games: 'Fill your basket' fair compensation beyond n = 16 (OEIS A392305) and the 3-basket guaranteed win beyond n = 14 (A391538, conjectured formula)
compute_profile: laptop-hours (exact minimax with memoisation over (remaining-coin set, sorted 3-basket sums) states plus alpha-beta or decision-version search; about 2^n * P^2/12 states before pruning; a rough estimate, not measured)
statement: Two perfect-information games on coins worth 1..n and three baskets, both by Ruediger Jehn. (1) 'Fill your basket' (A392305, keywords nonn,more, added Jan 06 2026): each of n turns the presenter chooses one of three baskets and the placer puts one remaining coin of their choice into it; at the end the placer scores the largest basket sum and the presenter the second largest; a(n) is the compensation paid to the presenter that makes the game a draw under optimal play, i.e. the minimax value of (largest - second largest). Known for n = 1..16: 1, 1, 1, 2, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 4, 4, 5, 5, 5, 6, 6. (2) A391538 (keywords nonn,more, Dec 12 2025): each turn the opponent chooses one of three baskets and the player puts a coin of their choice into it; at the end the player takes the largest basket; a(n) is the sum the player can guarantee. Known for n = 1..14: 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 11, 14, 17, 21, 25, 29, 34, 39, 44, with the entry's CONJECTURED formula a(n) = floor(n(n-1)/6) + n for n > 4 (it is a problem from the Mathekalender 2025 'Game of Chests' challenge by F. Niessen and S. Rathke). The 2-basket version A391537 has a proved closed form floor(n(n-1)/4) + n and is not a target. OPEN as of 2026-10-14: no term beyond n = 16 (A392305) or n = 14 (A391538), and the A391538 formula is unproved. The earlier page review could not retrieve the OEIS sources (HTTP 403), so the sequence frontiers and formula status remain input-reported.
success_criterion: CONFIRMED: the exact values of A392305(17), A392305(18), A392305(19), A392305(20) (K = 4 new terms; direction: new terms) under the entry's definition (presenter chooses the basket, then the placer chooses the coin, each turn; payoff = largest basket sum minus second-largest; placer maximises, presenter minimises; a(n) is that minimax value), each with a game certificate: a placer strategy table guaranteeing margin >= a(n) against every presenter choice AND a presenter strategy table holding the margin <= a(n) against every placer choice, both checked by an independent program that walks the (memoised) game graph exhaustively; plus exact reproduction of A392305 for n = 1..16. The terms must not already be in the OEIS entry, its b-file or edit history at verification time. Submitting to the OEIS is an action for the human only.

partial_wins.statement: A391538 for every n from 15 through 22 with the same two-sided certificate (opponent strategy capping the player's guaranteed sum at a(n), player strategy achieving it), reproducing n = 1..14; this confirms the conjectured formula floor(n(n-1)/6) + n on that range or refutes it at the first n where it fails (a certified counterexample to the formula as stated in the entry).
A392305(17) and A392305(18) only, with the two-sided certificate and calibration.

verification_method: Independent minimax from the definition, memoised on (frozen set of remaining coins, sorted basket sums); a terminal state scores largest minus second largest (A392305) or the largest sum (A391538). For a claimed value v, run two decision searches: 'can the placer force margin >= v' (must be true) and 'can the placer force margin >= v + 1' (must be false); each search returns a strategy table (the placer's move per reachable state for the first, the presenter's basket per reachable state for the second) that a third short program checks by exhaustive play-out against all replies. Calibrate on all published terms first. Exact integers throughout.
status_checked: 2026-10-14; historical proposal date preserved. No fresh source request was made during final preparation. The earlier page review could not retrieve the OEIS sources (HTTP 403), so the sequence frontiers and formula status remain input-reported.
angles: Decision version with a known bracket: the terms move by at most 1 per step so far, so test v = a(n-1) and a(n-1) + 1 first; each test is a boolean AND-OR search with heavy pruning.
Canonicalise the three sums by sorting; baskets with equal sums are interchangeable, which also prunes the presenter's choices.
Order the placer's coin choices largest-first and the presenter's baskets smallest-sum-first for early cutoffs.

For A391538, compare optimal play against Jehn's stated strategy (spread the first n-1 coins as evenly as possible over the three baskets, keep coin n for last); the first n where an even split of 1..n-1 into three parts is impossible is where to look for a formula failure.
pitfalls: In A392305 the placer scores the LARGEST basket and the presenter the SECOND largest; the third basket scores for nobody.
The presenter moves first in each turn (chooses the basket), then the placer chooses the coin; reversing this order is a different game.
A392305 is a margin game; do not compute the placer's guaranteed sum (that is A391538, a different payoff).
A391538's formula is labelled conjectured in the entry; matching it for n <= 14 is not evidence for larger n.
Memoisation keys must include the multiset of basket sums, not just their total.
